questions.question: What is the difference between rehearsing and refining? Why is refinement essential?

points.text: Rehearsing is learning and practising the piece; refining is making deliberate, specific improvements based on observation and feedback. Refinement is essential because running a piece repeatedly embeds mistakes — refinement identifies and fixes them.

questions.question: Describe how you would ensure smooth transitions between scenes in a devised piece.

points.text: Plan transitions as part of the drama: use movement, sound, lighting or narration to bridge scenes. Rehearse transitions until they are as precise as the scenes themselves. Never have blackouts with silence unless deliberately chosen.

questions.question: How can pacing and timing affect the audience's experience of a key dramatic moment?

points.text: A slow build creates tension; a sudden change creates shock; a well-timed pause lets the audience absorb significance. Pacing controls emotional engagement — the same moment at different speeds creates completely different effects.
